subject: Polity
description: NITI Aayog — composition, role, replacement of Planning Commission, governing council, three-year action agenda, NDC, Aspirational Districts.

questions.stem: NITI AAYOG was established to REPLACE the:
questions.explanation: NITI AAYOG (National Institution for Transforming India) — established 1 JANUARY 2015 by Cabinet Resolution under PM NARENDRA MODI; REPLACED the PLANNING COMMISSION (1950-2014). KEY DIFFERENCES from Planning Commission: (1) PLANNING COMMISSION — top-down centralized planning, controlled fund allocation. (2) NITI AAYOG — facilitator + think-tank role; cooperative federalism approach; states play stronger role. (3) PLANNING COMMISSION had quasi-financial powers; NITI Aayog has NONE (all financial powers to FINANCE MINISTRY). STRUCTURE: (1) CHAIRPERSON — PRIME MINISTER. (2) GOVERNING COUNCIL — all CMs + Lt Governors of UTs. (3) REGIONAL COUNCILS — formed for specific issues spanning multiple states. (4) VICE-CHAIRPERSON — appointed by PM (e.g., currently Suman Bery). (5) FULL-TIME MEMBERS, PART-TIME, EX-OFFICIO members. (6) SPECIAL INVITEES. (7) CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER — fixed tenure, secretary-rank. KEY FUNCTIONS: (1) Cooperative federalism. (2) Bottom-up planning. (3) Strategic + technical advice. (4) Developing 3-year action agenda, 7-year strategy, 15-year vision. (5) Monitoring + evaluation of govt schemes. STATUS: NEITHER constitutional NOR statutory — just an EXECUTIVE BODY (Cabinet Resolution); same status as Planning Commission was. UPSC angle: HUGE topic for Mains GS-2 (governance, federalism). PYQ FREQUENCY: NITI Aayog basics in UPSC, MPSC, state PSC 1-2× per cycle.

questions.stem: Who is the CHAIRPERSON of NITI Aayog?
questions.explanation: PRIME MINISTER is the EX-OFFICIO CHAIRPERSON of NITI Aayog. The PM also CHAIRS the GOVERNING COUNCIL (which includes all CMs + UT Lt Governors). RATIONALE: high-level policy-making body; PM-led ensures top-down + central role. KEY POSITIONS in NITI Aayog: (1) CHAIRPERSON — PM (Narendra Modi). (2) VICE-CHAIRPERSON — PM-appointed, holding rank of Cabinet Minister. CURRENT (April 2026): SUMAN BERY (since May 2022; succeeded Rajiv Kumar). PAST: ARVIND PANAGARIYA (2015-17), Rajiv Kumar (2017-22), Suman Bery. (3) FULL-TIME MEMBERS — 4-5 currently; rank of Minister of State. (4) PART-TIME MEMBERS — up to 2 from leading research bodies, universities. (5) EX-OFFICIO MEMBERS — up to 4 Union Ministers nominated by PM. (6) SPECIAL INVITEES — eminent experts, specialists nominated by PM. (7) CEO — secretary-rank IAS officer, 5-year fixed term. CURRENT: B.V.R. SUBRAHMANYAM (since Feb 2023). KEY GOVERNING COUNCIL MEETINGS: held annually; all CMs + UT Lt Govs gather; major federal policy decisions. NITI AAYOG GOVERNING COUNCIL meets FACE-TO-FACE with PM — major occasion for state-Centre coordination. UPSC angle: governance + federalism (cooperative federalism); GS-2. PYQ FREQUENCY: NITI Aayog leadership in UPSC, MPSC 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: ASPIRATIONAL DISTRICTS PROGRAMME (launched 2018) is administered by:
questions.explanation: ASPIRATIONAL DISTRICTS PROGRAMME (ADP) — launched JANUARY 2018; administered by NITI AAYOG. AIM: rapidly TRANSFORM 112 most-backward districts of India by enhancing development indicators. SELECTION: districts ranked using 49 KEY PERFORMANCE INDICATORS (KPIs) across 5 themes: (1) HEALTH & NUTRITION (~30%). (2) EDUCATION (30%). (3) AGRICULTURE & WATER (~20%). (4) FINANCIAL INCLUSION & SKILL (5%). (5) BASIC INFRASTRUCTURE (15%). MONTHLY 'DELTA RANKING' — comparing relative improvement; states + DMs compete. EARLY SUCCESS: many ADP districts have improved on multiple KPIs faster than national/state averages. KEY DISTRICTS: in BIHAR (12 ADPs — most), JHARKHAND (19 — most as % of state), CHHATTISGARH (10), UP (8), MP, WB, ODISHA. ADP EXTENDED to ASPIRATIONAL BLOCKS PROGRAMME (ABP) — launched 7 January 2023; covers 500 'most backward blocks' across India. APPROACH: 'CONVERGENCE + COLLABORATION + COMPETITION' — convergence of central + state schemes; collaboration with Centre + state + DM; competition among districts. UPSC angle: development administration + governance + federalism (cooperative). PYQ FREQUENCY: ADP/ABP in UPSC PT, Mains GS-2 development administration; SSC GA — 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: NITI AAYOG'S vision document covers a planning period of:
questions.explanation: NITI AAYOG's PLANNING DOCUMENTS structure: (1) 15-YEAR VISION DOCUMENT — long-term perspective. (2) 7-YEAR STRATEGY DOCUMENT — medium-term roadmap. (3) 3-YEAR ACTION AGENDA — short-term, immediately actionable. CONTRAST WITH PLANNING COMMISSION: had 5-YEAR PLANS (1st: 1951-56 to 12th: 2012-17). 12th Plan was the LAST 5-Year plan; from 2017 onwards, India follows NITI Aayog's 3-7-15 framework instead of 5-year plans. WHY 5-Year Plans were abandoned: (1) Critique that they were too rigid for fast-changing economy. (2) Excessive central control — clashed with cooperative federalism. (3) Implementation often diverged from plan. (4) Soviet-style planning seen as outdated post-1991 liberalization. INDIA'S 5-YEAR PLAN HISTORY (memorize for UPSC): (1) 1st (1951-56) — agriculture, irrigation. (2) 2nd (1956-61) — heavy industry (Mahalanobis model). (3) 3rd (1961-66) — followed by 'Plan Holiday' 1966-69 (3 ad-hoc annual plans due to wars + drought). (4) 4th (1969-74). (5) 5th (1974-79) — abandoned 1978; 'Rolling Plan' 1978-80. (6)-(11) — 1980-2012. (7) 12TH (2012-17) — LAST 5-Year plan; achievements: GDP growth ~7% (intended 9%), poverty reduction. UPSC angle: economic planning HISTORY in GS-3; reforms post-1991. PYQ FREQUENCY: NITI Aayog planning structure in UPSC, MPSC 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: NITI Aayog releases the SDG INDIA INDEX which measures progress on:
questions.explanation: SDG INDIA INDEX — annual report by NITI Aayog (since 2018) measuring INDIA's PROGRESS on 17 SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT GOALS (SDGs) adopted by UN in 2015 (TARGET YEAR 2030). MEASURES STATES + UTs against ~100 indicators. SDG 2030 GOALS (memorize summary): (1) NO POVERTY. (2) ZERO HUNGER. (3) GOOD HEALTH. (4) QUALITY EDUCATION. (5) GENDER EQUALITY. (6) CLEAN WATER & SANITATION. (7) AFFORDABLE & CLEAN ENERGY. (8) DECENT WORK & ECONOMIC GROWTH. (9) INDUSTRY, INNOVATION, INFRASTRUCTURE. (10) REDUCED INEQUALITIES. (11) SUSTAINABLE CITIES. (12) RESPONSIBLE CONSUMPTION & PRODUCTION. (13) CLIMATE ACTION. (14) LIFE BELOW WATER. (15) LIFE ON LAND. (16) PEACE, JUSTICE, INSTITUTIONS. (17) PARTNERSHIPS. INDIA's SDG SCORES (2023-24 edition): national score ~71/100; significant variation across states. KERALA, TAMIL NADU consistently top; BIHAR, JHARKHAND need most improvement. NITI also releases other indices: (1) HEALTH INDEX. (2) SCHOOL EDUCATION QUALITY INDEX. (3) WATER MANAGEMENT INDEX. (4) DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION INDEX. (5) STATE ENERGY & CLIMATE INDEX. UPSC angle: SDG progress is regular feature in PT current affairs + Mains GS-2/3. INDIA'S INTL CLIMATE PLEDGES: NDC under Paris Agreement — net zero by 2070 (announced COP26 Glasgow 2021); 50% RE by 2030; non-fossil 50%. PYQ FREQUENCY: SDGs + India SDG Index in UPSC PT/Mains 1-2× per cycle.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a body established under the Constitution?
questions.explanation: NITI AAYOG is NEITHER CONSTITUTIONAL NOR STATUTORY — created by CABINET RESOLUTION (1 January 2015); could be modified or abolished by simple cabinet decision. KEY CATEGORIZATION of bodies (memorize for UPSC): (1) CONSTITUTIONAL BODIES — created by Constitution itself. EXAMPLES: ELECTION COMMISSION (Art 324), UPSC (Art 315), STATE PSCs (Art 315), FINANCE COMMISSION (Art 280), CAG (Art 148), ATTORNEY GENERAL (Art 76), Advocate General of state (Art 165), NATIONAL COMMISSION FOR SCs/STs/BCs (Arts 338, 338A, 338B), GST COUNCIL (Art 279A — added 2016 via 101st Amendment), etc. (2) STATUTORY BODIES — created by ACTS of PARLIAMENT. EXAMPLES: NHRC (Protection of Human Rights Act 1993), NCW (NCW Act 1990), CIC (RTI Act 2005), CVC (CVC Act 2003), CBI (Delhi Special Police Establishment Act 1946), Lokpal (Lokpal Act 2013), NGT (NGT Act 2010), TRAI (TRAI Act 1997), SEBI (SEBI Act 1992), RBI (RBI Act 1934). (3) EXECUTIVE BODIES — created by EXECUTIVE order/cabinet resolution. EXAMPLES: NITI AAYOG (2015), Planning Commission (1950-2014), CCI (Competition Commission, mostly statutory but had executive elements), various task forces. NITI AAYOG'S VULNERABILITY: lacking constitutional/statutory backing means future government could abolish or modify it without legislative process. UPSC angle: 'Discuss the status of NITI Aayog vis-à-vis Planning Commission' — frequent essay/short-answer topic. PYQ FREQUENCY: body classification in UPSC PT, MPSC 1-2× per cycle.

questions.stem: The first VICE-CHAIRPERSON of NITI Aayog (2015-2017) was:
questions.explanation: ARVIND PANAGARIYA — first Vice-Chairperson of NITI Aayog (Jan 2015 - Aug 2017). BACKGROUND: Indian-American economist, Professor at Columbia University, NYU; Chief Economist of ADB previously; advocate of pro-market liberalization. KEY CONTRIBUTIONS during NITI tenure: (1) Established initial institutional framework. (2) Drafted the 3-year action agenda. (3) Advised on demonetization (Nov 2016 — though policy made by govt). (4) Pushed for ease-of-doing-business reforms. RETURNED to Columbia University 2017 + advisor positions. RECENT: appointed Chairman of 16TH FINANCE COMMISSION (December 2023; term 2026-2031, recommendations for 2026-27 to 2030-31 transfers). NITI AAYOG VC SUCCESSION: (1) Arvind Panagariya (2015-17). (2) Rajiv Kumar (2017-22). (3) Suman Bery (May 2022 onwards). FAMOUS NITI AAYOG figures: (a) BIBEK DEBROY — initially full-time member; later chair of Economic Advisory Council to PM (EAC-PM). (b) RAMESH CHAND — agriculture expert. (c) V.K. SARASWAT — DRDO ex-DG. NITI AAYOG GOVERNING COUNCIL recent: 9th meeting July 2024 — discussed 'Vikasit Bharat 2047' vision. UPSC angle: NITI Aayog leadership + recent reforms in GS-2. PYQ FREQUENCY: NITI VC succession in UPSC, MPSC 1× per 2 cycles. EXAMINER MINDSET (UPSC-level): tests current-affairs depth on key institutional figures.
